news.title: Ben White reveals heartbreaking reaction to missing World Cup and response to England boos
news.lede: Ben White revealed missing the last World Cup left him in tears. The Arsenal defender, 29, is famed for quitting the England camp in Qatar in 2022. But White’s reaction to missing out last summer through injury paints a very different picture of a player who insists it is still his dream to play for his country in a major tournament. White was exiled from the England set-up for four years until Thomas Tuchel brought him back in March, only for injury to ruin his chances of going to the United States.

news.title: Nigeria's U-17 Women's World Cup triumph adds to Africa's remarkable history of global youth football success
news.lede: Nigeria's historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026 has added another remarkable chapter to Africa's history of success in global youth football, making the Flamingos the first African women's team to win a FIFA world title at any age level. The Nigerians defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday's final in Rabat, becoming the latest African team to conquer the world stage and following a tradition established more than four decades ago by the country's Golden Eaglets. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku secured a landmark victory for Nigeria, who held off a late Japanese fightback to claim the trophy for the first time. The triumph represents a major breakthrough for African women's football, extending the continent's record of success in FIFA youth tournaments beyond the men's game.

news.title: Moroccan political figures slam Spanish opposition leader’s World Cup threats
news.lede: Moroccan political figures have criticized Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of Spain’s conservative People’s Party, after he threatened to withdraw Spain from co-hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup if the country is not awarded the tournament’s final. Their reactions come as Spain prepares for early elections on November 29, with several Moroccan political figures calling for the joint tournament, hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, to be kept out of political disputes. Unified Socialist Party: Feijóo’s remarks are electioneering. Jamal El Asri, secretary-general of the Unified Socialist Party and a member of the Left Alliance, described the Spanish right’s statements as political maneuvering linked to the election campaign.

news.title: NFF hails Flamingos’ historic World Cup triumph as heroines return to Nigeria
news.lede: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has described the Flamingos’ triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup as magnificent, as the victorious team returned to Nigeria to a warm reception following their historic achievement in Morocco. Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, NFF’s acting general secretary, and members of the federation’s management visited the players at their hotel in Abuja on Monday, where they praised the team’s discipline, hard work and determination in winning Nigeria’s first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title. Edit: How Flamingos defied Nigerian football’s troubles to conquer the world. Ikpeme conveyed the appreciation of the federation and the federal government, saying the players had elevated Nigeria’s standing in world football.

news.title: Kane and Bellingham air strong views in England World Cup review
news.lede: Kane and Bellingham made their views clear at the review. England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting. As BBC Sport reported in September, the Football Association (FA) process included canvassing the opinions of the squad - and it has emerged that took place at a 'full and frank' meeting with head coach Thomas Tuchel at the start of the September international break. BBC Sport has been told the squad feel that now they have been able to have their say, they can move on from their heartbreak in Atlanta on 15 July.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Messi returns to FIFPRO World 11, Ballon d'Or winner Kane misses out
news.lede: Nov 9 (Reuters) - Lionel Messi returned ⁠to the FIFPRO Men's World 11 for a record-extending 18th selection on Monday, ⁠but Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane was a surprise omission from the ‌team chosen by professional players from 73 countries. Messi, who announced his international retirement in August after helping Argentina reach the World Cup final and continues to play club football for Inter Miami, was named in ​the World 11 for the first time since 2023. The ⁠39-year-old was selected in a forward ⁠line alongside Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal. Lamine, ⁠19, ‌became the first player to earn two World 11 selections before turning 20 after also making last year's team.

news.title: Flamingos: 5 records Nigeria broke at 2026 U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Published on 9 Nov 2026 at 17:32 by Imhonlamhen. Nigeria’s Flamingos made history on Saturday, November 7, after beating Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku secured Nigeria’s first title in the competition and made them the first African nation to win the women’s U-17 World Cup. The victory also ended Africa’s wait for a FIFA women’s world title at any level.
